chapter.li: LEChapter10 Verse1 Now these are the words that Amulek preached unto the people who were in the land of Ammonihah, saying, VerseEnd Verse2 I am Amulek. I am the son of Gidanah, who was the son of Ishmael, who was a descendant of Aminadi; and it was that same Aminadi who interpreted the writing which was upon the wall of the temple, which was written by the finger of God. VerseEnd Verse3 And Aminadi was a descendant of Nephi, who was the son of Lehi, who came out of the land of Jerusalem, who was a descendant of Manasseh, who was the son of Joseph, who was sold into Egypt by the hands of his brethren. VerseEnd Verse4 And behold, I am also a man of no small reputation among all those who know me; yea, and behold, I have many kindred and friends. And I have also acquired much riches by the hand of my industry. VerseEnd Verse5 Nevertheless, after all this, I have never known much of the ways of the Lord, and his mysteries and marvelous power. I said I never had known much of these things, but behold, I mistake, for I have seen much of his mysteries and his miraculous power, yea, even in the preservation of the lives of this people. VerseEnd Verse6 Nevertheless, I did harden my heart, for I was called many times and I would not hear. Therefore, I knew concerning these things, yet I would not know. Therefore, I went on rebelling against God in the wickedness of my heart, even until the fourth day of this seventh month, which is in the tenth year of the reign of our judges. VerseEnd

Verse7 As I was journeying to see a very near kindred, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared unto me and said, Amulek, return to 2PSI thine own house, for 2PSI thou shalt feed a prophet of the Lord, yea, a holy man who is a chosen man of God; for he has fasted many days because of the sins of this people, and he is an hungered. And 2PSI thou shalt receive him into 2PSI thy house and feed him. And he shall bless 2PSI thee and 2PSI thy house, and the blessing of the Lord shall rest upon 2PSI thee and 2PSI thy house. VerseEnd

Verse8 And it came to pass that I obeyed the voice of the angel and returned towards my house. And as I was a going thither, I found the man whom the angel said unto me, 2PSI Thou shalt receive into 2PSI thy house; and behold, it was this same man who has been speaking unto 2PP you concerning the things of God. VerseEnd Verse9 And the angel said unto me, He is a holy man. Wherefore, I know he is a holy man because it was said by an angel of God. VerseEnd Verse10 And again I know that the things whereof he hath testified are true. For behold, I say unto 2PP you that as the Lord liveth, even so he hath sent his angel to make these things manifest unto me; and this he has done while this Alma hath dwelt at my house. VerseEnd Verse11 For behold, he hath blessed mine house; he hath blessed me, and my women, and my children, and my father, and my kinsfolks — yea, even all my kindred hath he blessed. And the blessing of the Lord hath rested upon us according to the words which he VerseEnd spake.

Verse12 And now when Amulek had spoken these words, the people began to be astonished, seeing there was more than one witness who testified of the things whereof they were accused, and also of the things which were to come, according to the spirit of prophecy which was in them. VerseEnd Verse13 Nevertheless, there were some among them who thought to question them, that by their cunning devices they might catch them in their words, that they might find witness against them, that they might deliver them to the judges, that they might be judged according to the law, and that they might be slain or cast into prison, according to the crime which they could make appear or witness against them. VerseEnd

Verse14 Now it was those men who sought to destroy them, who were lawyers, who were hired or appointed by the people to administer the law at their times of trial, or at the trials of the crimes of the people before the judges — VerseEnd Verse15 now these lawyers were learned in all the arts and cunning of the people, and this was to enable them that they might be skillful in their profession. VerseEnd Verse16 And it came to pass that they began to question Amulek, that thereby they might make him cross his words or contradict the words which he should speak. VerseEnd Verse17 Now they knew not that Amulek could know of their design; but it came to pass, as they began to question him, he perceived their thoughts. And he said unto them, O 2PP ye wicked and perverse generation, 2PP ye lawyers and hypocrites, for 2PP ye are laying the foundations of the Devil, for 2PP ye are laying traps and snares to catch the holy ones of God. VerseEnd Verse18 2PP Ye are laying plans to pervert the ways of the righteous and to bring down the wrath of God upon 2PP your heads, even to the utter destruction of this people. VerseEnd Verse19 Yea, well did Mosiah say, who was our last king, when he was about to deliver up the kingdom, having no one to confer it upon, causing that this people should be governed by their own voices — yea, well did he say that if the time should come that the voice of this people should cause iniquity, that is, if the time should come that this people should fall into transgression, they would be ripe for destruction. VerseEnd Verse20 And now I say unto 2PP you that well doth the Lord judge of 2PP your iniquities; well doth he cry unto this people by the voice of his angels, Repent 2PP ye, repent, for the kingdom of Heaven is at hand. VerseEnd Verse21 Yea, well doth he cry by the voice of his angels that I will come down among my people with equity and justice in my hands. VerseEnd Verse22 Yea, and I say unto 2PP you that if it were not for the prayers of the righteous who are now in the land, that 2PP ye would even now be visited with utter destruction. Yet it would not be by flood, as were the people in the days of Noah, but it would be by famine, and by pestilence, and the sword. VerseEnd Verse23 But it is by the prayers of the righteous that 2PP ye are spared. Now therefore, if 2PP ye will cast out the righteous from among 2PP you, then will not the Lord stay his hand, but in his fierce anger he will come out against 2PP you; then 2PP ye shall be smitten by famine, and by pestilence, and by the sword. And the time is soon at hand except 2PP ye repent. VerseEnd

Verse24 And now it came to pass that the people were more angry with Amulek, and they cried out, saying, This man doth revile against our laws, which are just, and our wise lawyers whom we have selected! VerseEnd Verse25 But Amulek stretched forth his hand and cried the mightier unto them, saying, O 2PP ye wicked and perverse generation! Why hath Satan got such great hold upon 2PP your hearts? Why will 2PP ye yield yourselves unto him, that he may have power over 2PP you to blind 2PP your eyes, that 2PP ye will not understand the words which are spoken according to their truth? VerseEnd Verse26 For behold, have I testified against 2PP your law? 2PP Ye do not understand. 2PP Ye say that I have spoken against 2PP your law, but I have not; but I have spoken in favor of 2PP your law, to 2PP your condemnation. VerseEnd Verse27 And now behold, I say unto 2PP you that the foundation of the destruction of this people is beginning to be laid by the unrighteousness of 2PP your lawyers and 2PP your judges. VerseEnd

Verse28 And now it came to pass that when Amulek had spoken these words, the people cried out against him, Now we know that this man is a child of the Devil! For he hath lied unto us, for he hath spoken against our law and now he says that he has not spoken against it! VerseEnd Verse29 And again he has reviled against our lawyers and our judges, etc. VerseEnd Verse30 And it came to pass that the lawyers put it into their hearts that they should remember these things against him. VerseEnd Verse31 And there was one among them whose name was Zeezrom. Now he was the foremost to accuse Amulek and Alma, he being one of the most expert among them, having much business to do among the people. VerseEnd Verse32 Now the object of these lawyers was to get gain, and they gat gain according to their employ. VerseEnd

LEChapter11 Verse1 Now it was in the law of Mosiah that every man who was a judge of the law, or those who were appointed to be judges, should receive wages according to the time which they labored to judge those who were brought before them to be judged. VerseEnd

Verse2 Now if a man oweth another, and he would not pay that which he did owe, he was complained of to the judge; and the judge executed authority and sent forth officers, that the man should be brought before him. And he judged the man according to the law and the evidences which were brought against him; and thus the man was compelled to pay that which he owed, or be striped, or be cast out from among the people as a thief and a robber. VerseEnd Verse3 And the judge receiveth for his wages according to his time: a senine of gold for a day, or a senum of silver, which is equal to a senine of gold. And this is according to the law which was given. VerseEnd

Verse4 Now these are the names of the different pieces of their gold and of their silver according to their value; and the names are given by the Nephites. For they did not reckon after the manner of the Jews who were at Jerusalem, neither did they measure after the manner of the Jews; but they altered their reckoning and their measure according to the minds and the circumstances of the people, in every generation until the reign of the judges, they having been established by king Mosiah. VerseEnd

Verse5 Now the reckoning is thus: a senine of gold, a seon of gold, a shum of gold, and a limnah of gold. VerseEnd Verse6 A senum of silver, an amnor of silver, an ezrum of silver, and an onti of silver. VerseEnd Verse7 A senum of silver was equal to a senine of gold, and either for a measure of barley, and also for a measure of every kind of grain. VerseEnd Verse8 Now the amount of a seon of gold was twice the value of a senine. VerseEnd Verse9 And a shum of gold was twice the value of a seon. VerseEnd Verse10 And a limnah of gold was the value of them all. VerseEnd Verse11 And an amnor of silver was as great as two senums. VerseEnd Verse12 And an ezrum of silver was as great as four senums. VerseEnd Verse13 And an onti was as great as all of them. VerseEnd Verse14 Now this is the value of the lesser numbers of their reckoning: VerseEnd Verse15 a shiblon is half of a senum; therefore, a shiblon for a half a measure of barley. VerseEnd Verse16 And a shilum is a half of a shiblon. VerseEnd Verse17 And a leah is the half of a shilum. VerseEnd Verse18 Now an antion of gold is equal to three shiblons. VerseEnd Verse19 Now this is their number according to their reckoning. VerseEnd

Verse20 Now it was for the sole purpose to get gain, because they received their wages according to their employ, therefore they did stir up the people to riotings and all manner of disturbances and wickedness, that they might have more employ, that they might get money according to the suits which were brought before them; therefore, they did stir up the people against Alma and Amulek. VerseEnd Verse21 And this Zeezrom began to question Amulek, saying, Will 2PSF ye answer me a few questions which I shall ask 2PSF you? Now Zeezrom was a man who was expert in the devices of the Devil, that he might destroy that which was good; therefore, he said unto Amulek, Will 2PSF ye answer the questions which I shall put unto 2PSF you? VerseEnd Verse22 And Amulek said unto him, Yea, I will, if they be according to the spirit of the Lord which is in me; for I shall say nothing which is contrary to the spirit of the Lord. And Zeezrom said unto him, Behold, here are six onties of silver, and all these will I give unto 2PSI thee if 2PSI thou wilt deny the existence of a supreme being. VerseEnd

Verse23 Now Amulek said, O 2PSI thou child of hell, why tempt 2PSF ye me? Knowest 2PSI thou that the righteous yieldeth to no such temptations? VerseEnd Verse24 Believest 2PSI thou that there is no God? I say unto 2PSF you, nay, 2PSI thou knowest that there is a God; but 2PSI thou lovest that lucre more than him. VerseEnd Verse25 And now 2PSI thou hast lied before God unto me; for 2PSI thou saidest unto me, Behold, these six onties, which are of great worth, I will give unto 2PSI thee, when 2PSI thou had it in 2PSI thy heart to retain them from me. And it was only 2PSI thy desires that I should deny the true and living God, that 2PSI thou mightest have cause to destroy me. And now behold, for this great evil 2PSI thou shalt have 2PSI thy reward. VerseEnd

Verse26 And Zeezrom said unto him, 2PSI Thou sayest there is a true and a living God? VerseEnd Verse27 And Amulek said, Yea, there is a true and a living God. VerseEnd Verse28 Now Zeezrom said, Is there more than one God? VerseEnd Verse29 And he answereth, No. VerseEnd Verse30 Now Zeezrom said unto him again, How knowest 2PSI thou these things? VerseEnd Verse31 And he said, An angel hath made them known unto me. VerseEnd Verse32 And Zeezrom said again, Who is he that shall come? Is it the Son of God? VerseEnd Verse33 And he said unto him, Yea. VerseEnd Verse34 And Zeezrom said again, Shall he save his people in their sins? And Amulek answered and said unto him, I say unto 2PSF you, he shall not; for it is impossible for him to deny his word. VerseEnd

Verse35 Now Zeezrom said unto the people, See that 2PP ye remember these things, for he said there is but one God, yet he said that the Son of God shall come, but he shall not save his people, as though he had authority to command God. VerseEnd Verse36 Now Amulek said again unto him, Behold, 2PSI thou hast lied; for 2PSI thou sayest that I speak as though I had authority to command God because I said he shall not save his people in their sins. VerseEnd Verse37 And I say unto 2PP you again that he cannot save them in their sins, for I cannot deny his word. And he hath said that no unclean thing can inherit the kingdom of Heaven. Therefore, how can 2PP ye be saved except 2PP ye inherit the kingdom of Heaven? Therefore, 2PP ye cannot be saved in 2PP your sins. VerseEnd Verse38 Now Zeezrom saith again unto him, Is the Son of God the very Eternal Father? VerseEnd Verse39 And Amulek said unto him, yea, he is the very Eternal Father of Heaven and earth and all things which in them is; he is the beginning and the end, the first and the last. VerseEnd Verse40 And he shall come into the world to redeem his people; and he shall take upon him the transgressions of those who believe on his name; and these are they that shall have eternal life, and salvation cometh to none else. VerseEnd Verse41 Therefore, the wicked remain as though there had been no redemption made, except it be the loosing of the bands of death. For behold, the day cometh that all shall rise from the dead, and stand before God, and be judged according to their works. VerseEnd

Verse42 Now there is a death which is called temporal death, and the death of Christ shall loose the bands of this temporal death, that all shall be raised from this temporal death; VerseEnd Verse43 the spirit and the body shall be reunited again in its perfect form; both limb and joint shall be restored to its proper frame, even as we now are at this time. And we shall be brought to stand before God, knowing even as we know now, and have a bright recollection of all our guilt. VerseEnd Verse44 Now this restoration shall come to all, both old and young, both bond and free, both male and female, both the wicked and the righteous. And even there shall not so much as a hair of their heads be lost; but all things shall be restored to its perfect frame, as it is now, or in the body, and shall be brought and be raigned before the bar of Christ the Son, and God the Father, and the holy spirit, which is one eternal God, to be judged according to their works, whether they be good or whether they be evil. VerseEnd

Verse45 Now behold, I have spoken unto 2PP you concerning the death of the mortal body, and also concerning the resurrection of the mortal body. I say unto 2PP you that this mortal body is raised to an immortal body, that is from death, even from the first death unto life, that they can die no more; their spirits uniting with their bodies, never to be divided, thus the whole becoming spiritual and immortal, that they can no more see corruption. VerseEnd

Verse46 Now when Amulek had finished these words, the people began again to be astonished; and also Zeezrom began to tremble. And thus ended the words of Amulek, or this is all that I have written. VerseEnd
